seeds.lower: segment bootstrap, numpy default_rng([20261103, place index]) per place (place index in run_tod_causal_citywide.places() order): {'Philadelphia': [20261103, 1], 'Austin 2009': [20261103, 2], 'Chicago 2015': [20261103, 4], 'Denver 2018': [20261103, 5], 'Saint Paul 2011': [20261103, 10]}

units.*_per100ac: extra homes per 100 lot acres a year (lower: edge effect at the district edge, 91 m bandwidth; central: 1/4-mile station-area effect)

methods.lower: Test 2 edge-test pooled floor (scripts/run_tod_causal_edge_expand.py, pool (a) original places, filter (a) level balance, main 91 m variant): 5 places Philadelphia; Austin 2009; Chicago 2015; Denver 2018; Saint Paul 2011. Each place's segment bootstrap re-run with its original seed stream and 2,000 draws; draws 1-1,000 equal the published 1,000 exactly. Pooled draw = mean of the 5 place draws. Homes = pooled x 44.8502 (15% x 4,874.1 / 100 x 5 x 1.2269). Pool membership fixed as published.
methods.central: Place bootstrap of the 11 D-11 places' 1/4-mile effects (run_tod_causal_central_pretrend.real_effect; New York and Philadelphia averaged over their rezonings), places resampled with replacement, mean per draw. Homes = mean x 299.0017.
methods.upper: central draws x 12,521 / 10,028 = 1.248604 (central scaled to a 15% district).

pairing: Lower draws come from a different procedure (segment bootstrap of edge places) and are independent of central and upper draws; pair them by row only as independent draws. Upper is perfectly tied to central (same row = same place resample).
caveat: The tool's displayed ranges for central (7,580 to 12,010) and upper (9,089 to 16,771) are leave-one-place-out ranges, not bootstrap intervals. The bootstrap 90% intervals here are wider. The lower's displayed range (2,279 to 5,791) is its bootstrap 90% interval.
